headline: 10 contracts catalogued across Ethereum, BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum and Blast (factories, a hook, Few token, RING token); no multisig/timelock/owner found; Hyperliquid L1 zero results.

findings.text: Block-explorer fetches could not be run because the tool-call budget ran out. Two explorer pages came back through search results instead: an Etherscan page tagged 'Ring Protocol: Few UNI Hook' (0xCF1E7189264a84D7454077dC713c3d11400de888) and a Blastscan RingToken page (0x25F233C3E3676f9e900a89644a3FE5404d643c84). A BscScan hit for 0x021988d2c89b1A9Ff56641b2F247942358FF05c9 is tagged 'RingFi', which looks like a different project, so it was excluded.

The legacy gitbook page https://ringprotocol.gitbook.io/ring/docs/deployments came back through search with a per-chain list of Ring Swap Factory and Few Factory addresses (ETH, BSC, Base, Arbitrum). Its table layout was flattened, so only addresses with an unambiguous adjacent label were catalogued. The newer docs.ring.exchange site and its contracts/overview page were not fetched.

The search listing for https://github.com/RingProtocol/audits shows three reports: ABDK (Hook v1.0), SlowMist, and BlockSec (ringcore v1.0). The direct fetch failed on the tool budget, so the PDFs were not opened and no scope-table addresses were extracted.

The RingProtocol GitHub org lists few-factory, few-v2-core, few-periphery, audits, universal-router and v4-periphery. No repo tree was walked and no commit SHA was pinned, so no deployment artifacts were extracted.

Addresses were catalogued for Ethereum (5), BNB Chain (1), Base (1), Arbitrum (2) and Blast (1). Hyperliquid L1 returned zero addresses from the sources tried. The gitbook page also mentions Unichain and Blast Sepolia, which are not in protocol.chains.

Factory addresses were found (Few Factory on Ethereum and Arbitrum; Ring Swap Factory on 4 chains). Their enumeration views (allPools, getPair, etc.) were not read because the fetch budget was exhausted, so no children were recorded.

Roles used are factory, token and other. No owner, admin, multisig, timelock or guardian address was surfaced in any source read. The Few UNI Hook's constructor arguments (from its Etherscan page) include a Uniswap v4 PoolManager and a Few wrapped token (derived from the ABI parameter names).
Only addresses with an adjacent label in a search-returned page body went into admin_addresses. Ambiguous or chain-unlabelled addresses were demoted to unknowns[].

rationale.verdict: Discovery slice, so grade is unknown by definition. Search-returned excerpts of the gitbook docs and two explorer pages were read; 10 addresses were catalogued. The fetch budget ran out before audits, GitHub trees, docs.ring.exchange and explorer or API reads could be done.

evidence.shows: Capability probe: web_fetch of protocol.website returned only a JS-required shell ('You need to enable JavaScript to run this app'), with no addresses or content.

Search-returned body of the legacy docs page 'Ring Protocol Contracts', which lists per-chain deployments. Labelled in the excerpt: ETH Ring Swap Factory 0xeb2A625B704d73e82946D8d026E1F588Eed06416; ETH Few Factory 0x7D86394139bf1122E82FDF45Bb4e3b038A4464DD; BSC Ring Swap Factory 0x4De602A30Ad7fEf8223dcf67A9fB704324C4dd9B; Base Ring Swap Factory 0x9BfFC3B30D6659e3D84754cc38865B3D60B4980E; Arbitrum Ring Swap Factory 0x1246Fa62467a9AC0892a2d2A9F9aafC2F5609442; Arbitrum Few Factory 0x974Cc3F3468cd9C12731108148C4DABFB5eE556F. Page age is about 383 days per the search metadata, so addresses may be superseded.

Search-returned Etherscan page tagged 'Ring Protocol: Few UNI Hook' (contract FewTokenHook). The constructor ABI takes IPoolManager _manager and IFewWrappedToken _fewToken. The constructor-args bytes decode (derived) to 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90 (PoolManager) and 0xe8e1f50392bd61d0f8f48e8e7af51d3b8a52090a (Few token).
Search-returned Blastscan token page titled 'Ring Protocol (ring)', contract name RingToken, with BlastManager.sol and IBlast sources.

Search-returned listing of the audits repo: ABDK_RingProtocol_Hook_v_1_0.pdf, SlowMist Audit Report - Ring Protocol_en-us.pdf, blocksec_ringcore_v1.0-signed.pdf. A direct fetch failed on the tool-call budget.
Search-returned GitHub org page listing 17 repos, including few-factory, few-v2-core, few-periphery, audits, universal-router (fork) and v4-periphery (fork).

Search-returned docs landing page: Few Protocol (wraps ERC-20s into canonical FewToken addresses), Uniswap v4 integration (FewToken and Few hooks), Ring Swap, and a 'Contract deployments' section covering factory, router, wrapper and Permit2 addresses by network.
Search-returned post stating RingSwap's underlying Few tokens are created and registered by the canonical Few Factory, and pointing to docs.ring.exchange for officially verified addresses.
Search-returned DefiLlama issue stating Ring Few TVL counts the underlying assets held by FewToken wrapper contracts, and linking docs.ring.exchange/contracts/overview as the contract map.

unknowns: D1: Direct explorer name-tag searches (etherscan.io searchHandler and per-chain explorers) were not performed because the web_fetch budget was exhausted. Only search-returned explorer pages for the Few UNI Hook and the Blast RingToken were seen.

D1-offchain: No on-chain read (explorer or defipunkd API) could be completed this run. The web_fetch of https://github.com/RingProtocol/audits failed on the tool budget, and no defipunkd surfacer URLs were pinned.

D1: BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum and Hyperliquid L1 explorer tag searches were not run. 0x021988d2c89b1A9Ff56641b2F247942358FF05c9 on BscScan is tagged RingFi, which looks like a different project, and was excluded.

D2: docs.ring.exchange/contracts/overview (the current deployments page, referenced by the DefiLlama issue) was not fetched. The gitbook page is stale, and its flattened table left the following addresses without a reliable chain or role: FewETHWrapper 0xAda6059b4F6244Acd8934095Ed0162C5Df6B5ebB, 0xf9d7ff2f6A0c3631A807199276a493Af8097916F and 0xCd31E6C1AD4c9E0E7F6A1f44583C038eaAaCf53F; Few Factory 0x1Fb6ef969D925f0B81245cE28F2cAD95b638CfCC, 0x455b20131D59f01d082df1225154fDA813E8CeE9 and 0x890509Fab3dD11D4Ff57d8471b5eAC74687E4C75; Permit2 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 and 0x787A81AF759621345c4D201667e893136CB41A2f; FewETHHook 0x12b504160222D66c38d916d9FbA11B613c51E888; FewWBTCHook 0x948922B055187c7366E71B876aB1242EBBAeA888; FewUSDCHook 0x1989CdAb2779ed83c0C81A5799FF6aF2e03c6888; FewDAIHook 0x90828f70070d84Ac5CDE145b27Ca75FDa6D02888. Next run should verify each on its explorer.

D2: The gitbook page also showed Unichain and Blast Sepolia sections and several Ring Swap Router entries whose addresses did not parse cleanly (some entries looked like init-code hashes, which are not addresses). None were recorded.
D3: The ABDK (Hook v1.0), SlowMist and BlockSec (ringcore v1.0) PDFs were not opened. Audit dates and in-scope address tables are unknown.

D4: No repo trees were walked (few-factory, few-v2-core, few-periphery) and no commit SHA was pinned, so there were no broadcast/ or deployments/ artifacts to read. protocol.github was not recorded in the context.

D5: chain Hyperliquid L1: zero addresses surfaced from the sources tried (website JS shell, gitbook search excerpt, org search). Ring Router and Ring Swap Router addresses were not recorded for any chain.
D5: chain Blast: only the RING token was found. The Blast Few Factory and Ring Swap Factory are unknown, and the X post mentions Blast winding down its network.
D6: Factory children (Few wrapped tokens via the Few Factory; pairs via the Ring Swap Factory) were not enumerated because no read-API fetch was possible. The cap of 50 children per factory applies.
D7: No owner, admin, proxy admin, multisig, timelock or guardian address was found for any contract. Upgradeability is unknown.
D8: Addresses seen only in search snippets without a clear chain or role label (see D2) were deliberately left out of admin_addresses.
D2: Governance forum, bug bounty and security contact were not found in the sources read. Voting token is unknown and probably not applicable.

protocol_metadata.about: Ring Protocol's Few Protocol layer wraps ordinary ERC-20 assets into canonical FewToken wrappers, created and registered through a per-network Few Factory. Ring Swap is an AMM whose pools hold these wrapped tokens, and Few hooks integrate the wrappers with Uniswap v4. Ring Few's TVL counts the underlying assets held by the FewToken wrapper contracts.
